title: Court Case Preparation — August 10, 2026
description: Complete study module for your 74th District Court hearing

sections.title: Your Case Overview
sections.content: Case: 74th District Court, Bay City. Case Number: 26-4144-SC. Date: Monday, August 10, 2026, 9:30 AM. Magistrate: Perry. Plaintiff: Jolene D. Wilcox. Incident: June 7, 2026 vehicle collision. Amount claimed: $5,664.68 (vehicle damage, towing, storage). Key fact: The mini-tort cap limits recovery to $3,000 for vehicle damage. The claim exceeds this cap. Towing and storage may be separately recoverable but must be proven reasonable. Both parties show GEICO on the UD-10 crash report, but the plaintiff has not provided proof of active insurance with her filing.

sections.title: Michigan Law Fundamentals
sections.content: Small claims jurisdiction: MCL 600.8401. Jurisdictional ceiling: $7,000 since January 1, 2024 (MCL 600.8401(e)). Statute of limitations: 3 years for tort claims (MCL 600.5805(2)). Burden of proof: plaintiff must prove damages by preponderance of evidence. Mini-tort (MCL 500.3135): Capped at $3,000 for accidents after July 1, 2020 (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). This is an AMOUNT DEFENSE — it limits recovery, not a dismissal. The plaintiff must prove: (1) she was 50% or less at fault, (2) her vehicle had no-fault insurance on June 7, 2026, (3) the damages were not covered by her own insurance. If she cannot prove active insurance, the mini-tort claim may be barred under MCL 500.3135(4)(e). The UD-10 crash report shows GEICO for both parties, but this is police-reported information — the plaintiff should produce proof of coverage (declarations page, policy document, or insurance card).

sections.title: Your Rights as Defendant
sections.content: Right to present evidence (bring all documents, photos, witnesses). Right to cross-examine witnesses (within informal hearing format). Right to request adjournment (NOT guaranteed — judge decides). NO ATTORNEY MAY APPEAR in small claims (MCL 600.8408(1)) — if you want a lawyer, case must be removed to general civil division before trial. Right to file counterclaim (must have independent legal basis and provable damages). Right to appeal magistrate decision to district judge within 7 days. Right to request the plaintiff produce proof of insurance. The UD-10 crash report is NOT conclusive proof of active coverage — officers only record what's on the card, they don't verify with the insurance company. Direct verification (declarations page, letter of coverage, claim check) is required to prove the policy was active on the date of the accident.

sections.title: What to Say
sections.content: SAFE: 'I'm here to respond to the claim.' 'The mini-tort cap limits recovery to $3,000 for vehicle damage. The claim exceeds this amount.' 'The plaintiff's claim is for mini-tort damages under MCL 500.3135. The mini-tort cap limits recovery to $3,000 for vehicle damage. The UD-10 crash report only shows what was on the insurance card — it does not verify the policy was active. I request direct verification from GEICO.' 'Your Honor, the UD-10 crash report only shows what the officer recorded from the insurance card. It does not verify the policy was active on June 7, 2026. I request that the plaintiff produce direct verification from GEICO — a declarations page, letter of coverage, or claim check.' 'Your Honor, if the plaintiff cannot produce direct proof that her policy was active on June 7, 2026, the mini-tort claim should be barred under MCL 500.3135(4)(e).' 'I applied my brakes at the stop sign.' 'I have documentation of my own damages.'

sections.title: What NOT to Say
sections.content: DO NOT: Admit fault (the police report shows your vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign). Rely on the '$3,000 means I can't be sued' theory — this is WRONG. The $3,000 is a mini-tort cap on recovery, NOT a jurisdictional ceiling. Make emotional statements. Discuss legal theories you can't support. Say anything about insurance without careful thought. Argue the plaintiff was uninsured — only argue she hasn't proven her policy was active. The UD-10 shows GEICO was listed, but that's not the same as proof the policy was in force.

sections.title: Court Procedure
sections.content: IMPORTANT: Both in-person AND Zoom are checked on your packet. Call the court (989-895-4232 or 989-895-4203) to CONFIRM before Monday. If in-person: arrive by 9:00 AM, check in with clerk, wait for case to be called. If Zoom: Meeting ID 946-661-3202, do NOT join early or late. Stand when speaking (if in-person). Address magistrate as 'Your Honor' or 'Magistrate Perry'. Present your response clearly. TAKE NOTES — there is NO court reporter and NO verbatim record (MCL 600.8411(2)). Your notes are the only record of what happened.

sections.title: Risk Assessment
sections.content: CRITICAL: The police report (UD-10, Officer Jacob Kirsch) states Unit 1 (your vehicle) failed to stop at the stop sign and caused the collision. This is documented evidence. The claim amount ($5,664.68) exceeds the mini-tort cap ($3,000). A finding against you on the mini-tort limits your exposure to $3,000 for vehicle damage. The claim also includes towing and storage which may be separately recoverable. Be prepared to respond to the stop-sign evidence without admitting fault.

sections.title: Mini-Tort Strategy
sections.content: The mini-tort claim is capped at $3,000 (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). The plaintiff claims $5,664.68, which exceeds the cap. Under the law: (1) You are only liable for up to $3,000 in vehicle damage under the mini-tort. (2) Towing and storage may be separately recoverable but must be proven reasonable and necessary. (3) The plaintiff must prove she had active no-fault insurance on June 7, 2026. (4) The UD-10 crash report is NOT proof of active coverage — it only shows the officer recorded what was on the insurance card. Officers do not call the insurance company to verify the policy was active. A policy could have been canceled before the accident. (5) The plaintiff must produce DIRECT VERIFICATION from GEICO (declarations page, letter of coverage, or claim check) to prove her policy was active on June 7, 2026. (6) If she cannot produce direct verification, the mini-tort claim may be barred entirely under MCL 500.3135(4)(e). Your strategy: State the mini-tort cap ($3,000 max), request direct proof of insurance from GEICO, challenge unreasonable towing/storage costs, present your own documentation of damages.

sections.title: Documents to Bring
sections.content: CRITICAL DOCUMENTS FOR COURT: (1) The 11-page filing/packet from plaintiff. (2) Case number: 26-4144-SC (write on sticky note). (3) Your insurance documents/policy. (4) Photos of vehicle damage (both cars if available). (5) Police/citation records from June 7 incident. (6) Your own repair estimates or receipts. (7) Any correspondence with insurance companies. (8) Notepad and pen — THERE IS NO COURT REPORTER. (9) This study guide — print the Quick Reference card. (10) arrive with organized folder, not loose papers.

sections.title: Courtroom Procedure
sections.content: SMALL CLAIMS PROCEDURE — WHAT HAPPENS WHEN: (1) Check-in: Arrive 30 minutes early, check in at clerk's window. Phone off, notes ready. (2) Call & Identification: Magistrate calls case number, both parties state names, both sworn in. Stand when speaking. (3) Plaintiff's Case: Plaintiff speaks FIRST for 5-8 minutes. She presents documents, calls witnesses. DO NOT INTERRUPT. Take notes. (4) Your Case: Magistrate turns to you. Give your planned response. You may ask the plaintiff questions. (5) Magistrate Questions: Magistrate probes both sides. Answer honestly, don't argue. (6) Closing: Short statements from both sides. Ask: 'Your Honor, may I make a brief closing statement?' (7) Decision: Magistrate rules immediately or takes under advisement (decision mailed). Either way, write down the result. 7-day appeal window. EXPECT 20-30 MINUTES TOTAL.

sections.title: How to Open
sections.content: YOUR OPENING — EXACT SCRIPT: 'Good morning, Your Honor. I'm Sophia Saitta, the defendant in this matter. I'm here to respond to the claim, and I'd like to give my account of what happened.' THAT'S IT. Name + purpose + readiness. Do NOT make a speech about yourself. Do NOT say what you do for a living unless it's relevant. The magistrate has 20 cases today. Competence and calm win, not credentials. If you want to mention your work, use it as a grounding line: 'I run a technology company, Your Honor, so I'm used to being organized — I want to assure you I've come prepared to be straightforward about what happened.'

sections.title: When You Speak — Argument Order
sections.content: ORDER OF ARGUMENTS — PSYCHOLOGY OF PERSUASION: (1) CONCEDE WHAT YOU CAN'T WIN: 'I don't deny the collision happened, and I don't deny Ms. Wilcox's car was damaged.' This buys maximum credibility. (2) PRESENT YOUR ACCOUNT: 'I applied my brakes at the stop sign. The absence of skid marks suggests the brakes may not have responded as expected. The police report captures one perspective — I'd like to present my account.' (3) CITE THE LAW: 'Under MCL 500.3135, any recovery for vehicle damage is capped at $3,000, reduced by comparative fault, and only to the extent not covered by insurance. The claim exceeds this cap.' (4) REQUEST SPECIFIC RELIEF: 'I ask that any recovery be reduced by the plaintiff's share of fault, capped at the $3,000 statutory limit, and only to the extent the damages are not covered by insurance.' Plant seeds of doubt through QUESTIONS, not accusations: 'I ask the court to weigh...' not 'She's wrong.'

sections.title: Your Closing Statement
sections.content: YOUR CLOSING — MEMORIZE THIS: 'Your Honor, I came here to be straightforward. I don't deny the collision happened, and I don't deny Ms. Wilcox's car was damaged. But I ask that you weigh the ambiguity in the physical scene against the report, that any recovery reflect that this was not solely my responsibility, that it be capped at the $3,000 statutory limit for vehicle damage, and that the towing and storage be supported by receipts and only to the extent not covered by insurance. Whatever you decide, I appreciate your time and consideration.' WHY THIS WORKS: It concedes what you can't win (buys credibility), restates your three winning points (comparative fault, cap, documented damages), and ends with grace and respect. End with thanks, not threats.

sections.title: Staying Calm Under Pressure
sections.content: NAVY SEAL CALM — HOW TO STAY CENTERED: (1) Box Breathing: In 4 counts, hold 4, out 4, hold 4. Repeat 5 times before entering. (2) Posture: Feet flat, back straight, hands still. Open, grounded posture projects confidence. Do NOT cross arms or fidget. (3) Eye Contact: Look at the magistrate when speaking and when they speak. Steady, not a stare-down. Strongest credibility signal. (4) Slow Down: Before answering, take one small breath and a half-second pause. You are never in a hurry. (5) Notepad: Write things down. It anchors you. (6) Mantra: 'I'm the calmest, most reasonable adult here.' (7) Reframe: This is capped at $3,000 — not life or death. You cannot lose your freedom. The downside is bounded. If you blank: 'Your Honor, I'd like a moment to check my notes.'

sections.title: Psychology of the Courtroom
sections.content: THE PSYCHOLOGY OF WINNING — FROM PSYCHE (Psychological Artisan): THE MAGISTRATE'S TRIFECTA: (1) Credibility — strategic concession + no over-claiming + calm correction + steady eyes. (2) Preparation — arrive early, organized documents, cite statute once precisely, take notes, have police report ready to hand up. (3) Reasonableness — frame every doubt as evidence, not accusation; concede the accident; treat plaintiff with courtesy; yield to court's authority. NEUTRALIZE THE VICTIM SCHEMA: You cannot beat 'I was hit' head-on — she IS the injured party. Do not try to make her the villain. Instead, win the AMOUNT and COMPARATIVE FAULT. Redirect from 'who's at fault' to 'what's fair and provable.' The victim schema wins sympathy; the cap and evidence win the number. BUILD YOUR 'HONEST, REASONABLE' SCHEMA: Concede something real early ('I don't dispute the accident happened') — the magistrate's brain files you as honest. Every subsequent denial is assimilated into that honest frame. The gratitude frame (thanking the court) activates reciprocity — the magistrate unconsciously wants to give the courteous party the benefit of the doubt. UNCONSCIOUS TRUST LEVERS (ranked): (1) Calm — edges out everything; a calm party is presumed honest. (2) Strategic concession — honesty signal. (3) Specificity — dates, dollar figures, details you recall. Vague people are suspicious; specific people are believed. (4) No weasel words — no 'maybe,' 'I guess,' 'possibly not.' State what you know firmly; mark what you don't know honestly. (5) Courtesy to the plaintiff — treated well, she does the work of making you look decent. (6) Respect for the bench — yield to magistrate's control, never argue. THE ONE MOVE THAT WINS: Make the magistrate's job easy. Give her a clean story, a clean number, and a reason to side with you she can defend. When a magistrate can rule for you AND point to the statute, she rules for you. Your job is to hand her that statute and that number without making it feel like a fight.

sections.title: Forbidden Moves — DO NOT DO THESE
sections.content: FORBIDDEN MOVES — READ BEFORE ENTERING: ❌ Interrupting anyone. ❌ Arguing with the magistrate. ❌ Admitting fault ('I ran the sign'). ❌ 'The brakes failed' — sounds like vehicle maintenance admission. ❌ 'She didn't brake' — speculation without evidence. ❌ 'She's lying' — inflammatory and unprofessional. ❌ 'She has no insurance' — UD-10 shows GEICO; say 'hasn't proven her policy was active.' ❌ 'I owe nothing' — loses credibility; you're conceding the collision happened. ❌ Reacting visibly to plaintiff's testimony. ❌ Rambling — you have ~3-5 minutes of speaking time. Be brief, be specific, be done.
